elements.element: Vendor may conduct no more than one audit in any twelve-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that Licensor may request no more than one audit in any twelve-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer at least 30 days’ prior written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires a written request but only says the audit must be permitted within 30 days after receipt. This allows the audit to occur immediately and does not provide 30 days’ prior notice.

elements.element: The audit must be conducted during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires the audit to be conducted during Licensee’s normal business hours.

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The clause requires an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional selected by mutual agreement.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The auditor must be bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor bears the audit cost unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear the audit costs only if the audit discovers an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon any discrepancy exceeding 5%, rather than specifically an underpayment exceeding 5%.

elements.element: The auditor must have no direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition on direct access to Licensee’s systems; limiting the audit to appropriate accounting records does not expressly bar such access.

elements.element: Vendor may conduct no more than one audit per year.
elements.evidence: The clause’s limit of one audit in any twelve-month period satisfies this frequency requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer at least 15 days’ prior notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Although the request must be written, the requirement to permit the audit within 30 days does not guarantee any minimum prior-notice period.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor bears the audit cost unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear the audit costs only if the audit discovers an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs for any discrepancy exceeding 5%, not only for an underpayment exceeding 10%.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested frequency, business-hours, independence, and confidentiality protections, but it does not create a minimum prior-notice period, does not prohibit direct systems access, and uses a broader 5% “discrepancy” cost-shifting trigger rather than the required underpayment trigger. It therefore reaches neither complete position. It also adds a non-interference requirement not contained in either position, so it is not minimal, although it does not contradict or displace unrelated commercial terms.
